title: Equal Experts fits on model but is too large to be a first design partner
content:
Equal Experts qualifies on structure and is held back on scale. The partner-network model means delivery runs through associates rather than a fixed bench, and the firm states technology agnosticism, so there is no proprietary platform whose position an application layer built on Powerhouse would threaten. Both are signals the screen is looking for.

The blocker is size: somewhere between 1,000 and 5,000 people is larger than a first design partner should be. What counts against a firm at that scale is not capability but decision latency and attention — a pilot gets allocated to a practice rather than to the people who would shape the product. The record marks it priority 2, next rather than now.

It stays in the pool because the agnosticism claim, if it holds, makes it a plausible second-wave route: once there is a reference implementation to point at, a partner network is an efficient way to spread it. The judgement here is about sequencing, not about fit.
